problem: The figure uses exactly the worked-example data (h₀ = 20 mm, h₁ = 15 mm, R = 300 mm, μ = 0.10) and shows a completed pass with a 5 mm draft and L = 38.7 mm. Worked example 1 proves with the same numbers that this pass is impossible (Δh = 5 mm > Δhmax = 3 mm). A student can read the figure as a pass that succeeds and then meet the example that says it fails.
fix: Keep the geometry but add a note to the figure, for example: 'Geometry only. At μ = 0.10 the bite limit is Δhmax = μ²R = 3 mm, so this 5 mm pass would need μ ≥ 0.13.' Or change the figure to a pass that satisfies the bite condition, e.g. h₀ = 18 mm, h₁ = 15 mm.

problem: 'The bite angle α is the angle between the entry point and the roll centre line' is vague. An angle is between two lines or planes, not between a point and a line; a student may not see which two lines to draw.
fix: The bite angle α is the angle at the centre of one roll between the radius drawn to the entry point of the strip and the line joining the centres of the two rolls.

where: Section 1 and formula box for L
problem: The text calls L the 'horizontal length' of the arc, but the formula box calls it the 'contact length along the arc'. These are two different lengths (projected length R sin α against arc length Rα), even though both come to about √(RΔh) for shallow bites, so the wording contradicts itself.
fix: Say once: 'L is the projected (horizontal) length of the contact arc, L ≈ √(RΔh).' Use the same words in the formula box: 'L is the projected contact length (mm)'.
